newsitem.title: POLAND: Strong dollar shoots down zloty, Polish depos soar.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar shoots down zloty, Polish depos soar.

text.p: The zloty fell against the basket of currencies as banks lenghtened currency positions to take advantage of the U.S. dollar's gains against major currencies in European trade, dealers said.

They said the zloty spent most of the session calmly tracking dollar/mark moves, but that most banks were looking to buy currencies at the end of the day to gain greater exposure to the dollar, which today hit highs around 1.5260 marks.
"At the end of the day the market was oriented toward corrency buyers, probably as banks lenghtened foreign currency positions," said Jaroslaw Dryski of Bank Slaski SA.

The zloty closed at 1.80/1.71 percent from the trading band centre against Wednesday's 1.91/1.87 percent on Wednesday and dealers said currency buying was likely more popular at the post-trade fixing session with the central bank.
The National Bank of Poland fixed the zloty at an average of 1.66 percent from parity, down from 1.93 percent yesterday.
The zloty closed at 2.8025/45 to the dollar, down two groszes from Wednesday's 2.7825/40. It was at 1.8405/25 to the mark, up from yesterday's 1.8450/60.
One-day rates soared as banks looked for cash to fine-tune required accounts before the end of the September reserve.
Overnight rates soared to 20.00/22.00 percent from yesterday's 19.50/19.55, while tomorrow/next rates rose to 20.30/22.30 percent from 19.30/19.80.
"Wednesday's reverse repo and NBP-bill sale drained the market of excess cash and many banks were short after large end-of-month paycheck outflows," said Tadeusz Kydel of BGZ SA.
"One can expect demand for cash will be very high tomorrow, the last trading day of the monthly reserve, because T/N rates were high today," Kydel added.
The September required reserve period ends on Sunday.
